The Eigenharp is an electronic instrument brand launched by the British company Eigenlabs; in essence it is a portable controller, and the sound is produced by the software it drives. In sounding classification it is a keyboard / electrophone / mechanical hybrid, Hornbostel–Sachs number 412/31/52. It has a blowpipe, a velocity-sensitive key matrix and strip controllers, and each key can be controlled like a six-way analogue joystick; the larger model also has percussion keys and a headphone output. When playing, the fingers on the keys, the breath and the strips control pitch, modulation and other parameters at the same time. It is mostly found among electronic music producers and bands, in modern composition and live performance.
艾根豎琴本身不直接發聲，而是作為控制器，聲音由其驅動的軟體產生。其鍵矩陣為速度敏: The Eigenharp does not sound by itself; it is a controller, and the sound is produced by the software it drives. Its key matrix is velocity-sensitive and highly expressive, and each key can be worked like a six-way analogue joystick, so that the player can bend the pitch, modulate or control other parameters of a single note independently. The blowpipe provides continuous breath-style control, and the strip controllers can be used for glissandi or parameter changes. Different models' numbers of keys, blowpipes, strips and percussion keys change how many notes and parameter layers can be controlled at once, so the timbre depends mainly on the software being driven and on how the player works each controller.
艾根豎琴由英國德文郡Eigenlabs推出，創辦人John Lambert曾為環: The Eigenharp was launched by Eigenlabs of Devon in the United Kingdom. The founder, John Lambert, had been a member of the ambient psychedelic dance group Shen, and because he felt that electronic instruments were less expressive than the guitar or the voice, he sold his internet company Hyperlink and set up Eigenlabs in 2001, completing the work after eight years of development. Alpha appeared in 2009, Pico in 2010 and Tau in 2012; the aim throughout was to combine keyboard, free reed, electrophone and mechanical interfaces into a portable controller whose sound is produced by software.
